requirement: Implement a transaction validation system and test harness that verifies specific exception types AND exact error message patterns with regex precision, preventing loose or absent match checks.
skeleton: process_withdrawal validator raising specific TransactionError subtypes and verify_exception_match test harness helper.
caption: A standard-library withdrawal validator and exception-matching harness that checks both the exact exception type and a regular-expression match on its message, with no third-party imports. TransactionError subclasses ValueError, and InsufficientFundsError and InvalidAccountStatusError both subclass TransactionError. process_withdrawal(balance, amount, status) raises InvalidAccountStatusError naming the status whenever the status is anything other than active, so frozen, closed, and pending accounts are all refused; raises a plain ValueError stating the amount must be strictly positive when the amount is zero or negative; raises InsufficientFundsError reporting the requested amount and balance to two decimals when the amount exceeds the balance; and otherwise returns the remaining balance. verify_exception_match(func, expected_type, exact_pattern) calls the function and catches only the expected type; it then applies re.search with the pattern to the message, returning True on a match and raising AssertionError naming the pattern and message, chained from the caught exception, when it does not match, so a regex is honoured rather than compared literally. Any other exception type raises AssertionError reporting the expected and actual type names, chained from that exception, and a call that raises nothing raises AssertionError reporting that the expected exception was not raised. The fixture asserts that withdrawing 40 from 100 leaves 60.0, that an overdraft matches an anchored pattern with decimal amounts, that a wrong pattern raises AssertionError reporting did not match, that a zero withdrawal checked for InsufficientFundsError raises AssertionError reporting Expected InsufficientFundsError, got ValueError, that a zero amount raises ValueError reporting strictly positive, and that a frozen account raises InvalidAccountStatusError naming frozen.

plan.intent: Validate withdrawals and check raised exceptions by exact type and message pattern
constraints: A status other than active raises InvalidAccountStatusError naming it
An amount above the balance raises InsufficientFundsError with both amounts to two decimals
The checker searches the message with the regex and raises AssertionError when it does not match
A different exception type, or no exception at all, raises AssertionError

rationale.teaches: An exception harness that checks the exact type and a regex match on the message, a withdrawal validator that rejects zero amounts, and a status check that only allows active accounts.
rationale.why: A harness that catches Exception or ignores the pattern passes on any error, so a wrong error type or message goes unnoticed. The fixture raises the wrong subtype and a near-miss message and expects the harness to fail.

ops.docstring: Validate withdrawals and assert that a call raises a matching exception.

ops.source:
class TransactionError(ValueError):
    """Base class for rejected transactions."""

class InsufficientFundsError(TransactionError):
    """Raised when a withdrawal exceeds the balance."""

class InvalidAccountStatusError(TransactionError):
    """Raised when the account status forbids withdrawals."""

candidates.why_wrong: Only the pattern's truthiness is checked, so any message passes as long as a pattern was given.
The pattern is compared by equality, so a regex like 'insufficient.*funds' never matches.
Zero amounts pass validation, so a withdrawal of 0 succeeds.
Exception is caught instead of the expected type, so a ValueError passes a check for InsufficientFundsError.
Only suspended accounts are rejected, so a closed or pending account can withdraw.
